svg.title: ETL & Data Ingestion
svg.desc: Proposed ETL detail for Enterprise AI Agent Sales and Risk System. This page is an architecture design, not a live database, Gmail, AWS or Snowflake integration. The internal database stays on the private network and is read through a read-only connector by an incremental export worker. Export uses a durable source watermark and stable keys, with bounded lookback or explicit backfills. Large exports are paginated and batched; no model queries the source. The source and all derived copies are processed only by enterprise-approved cloud services and models. Network egress restrictions, private connectivity where supported, least-privilege source permissions and a fail-closed model/tool allowlist enforce the approved processing boundary, including retrieved context, embeddings, evaluation, logs and traces. Approved Bedrock-hosted models may process authorized context through the AgentCore workflow; this does not mean the models are enterprise self-hosted. Model, region, data-retention and logging settings require enterprise approval. This diagram specifies controls to implement; it does not prove a deployed security guarantee. Gmail watch delivers mailbox-change notifications through Google Cloud Pub/Sub; it does not deliver complete email bodies. Google Pub/Sub is required on this Gmail push path even though the application backend uses AWS. API Gateway and an ingress Lambda verify the Google push identity and audience. The handler acknowledges only after durable SQS enqueue; it does not wait for API fetches, attachment parsing or LLMs. At-least-once deliveries are deduplicated using source and event identifiers. The worker uses Gmail history.list and messages.get to fetch changed content and attachments. API throttling honors Retry-After and uses bounded retry/backoff. Source cursors advance only after corresponding changes are durably saved, with concurrency control per mailbox. SQS visibility timeouts, partial-batch failure handling, bounded attempts and a dead-letter queue support recovery. Replayed notifications and out-of-order events cannot overwrite newer versions. S3 keeps raw source envelopes, fetched MIME or JSON and attachments under deterministic source/version keys. Version metadata preserves edits and deletion tombstones; retention and deletion requirements apply to derived copies too. Database row-level permissions and mailbox authorization are captured and enforced downstream, not replaced by an LLM label. Airflow owns micro-batch orchestration, retries and backfills; it is not one DAG per message. Airflow also schedules periodic source reconciliation, Gmail watch renewal before expiry and recovery when an incremental cursor expires. Source sync state and Airflow batch checkpoints are distinct durable records; mailbox sync cursor advancement does not wait for document indexing. A batch manifest in Snowflake selects unprocessed source versions, scoped by source, customer/project and received time, with bounded replay windows for late-arriving edits and explicit backfill ranges. Parse and Prepare runs on Airflow task workers or a configured task execution backend. It extracts permitted MIME and attachment content, normalizes encodings, preserves raw evidence and schema versions, and prepares bulk-loading files. S3 retains the raw archive. Bulk Load uses Snowflake COPY INTO for prepared records in working staging tables, not a permanent second raw archive. Snowflake is the compute engine for subsequent dbt transforms. Existing CRM tables and the analytics team's established Snowflake computation framework are reused. dbt compiles SQL executed by Snowflake and joins prepared operational changes with these governed CRM records. Incremental MERGE first deduplicates each incoming business/source key, applies source-version ordering and handles deletion tombstones; a unique_key config alone does not guarantee uniqueness. When a transformation depends on other project facts, changed-key propagation and late-data lookback select every affected project. Emails are evidence or proposed changes, not authoritative ERP commitments. Data Validation combines dbt tests and Great Expectations: schema, non-null/unique keys, source/project access metadata, freshness, counts, referential integrity and applicable units or currencies. Failed records or batches are quarantined with reason codes; no failed batch reaches the published serving version. An Airflow task retry never marks an unfinished batch complete. The publish operation atomically advances a Snowflake serving-version manifest only after required checks succeed, then commits the corresponding batch checkpoint. A failure after publication but before checkpoint commit is safe to replay: the batch/source version identities and MERGE operations are idempotent. CRM, Project Facts and Features are Snowflake serving tables/views joined with existing governed CRM records. Their downstream daily risk scoring also runs in Snowflake using an approved model; AWS SageMaker is reserved for training. Risk scores remain in Snowflake for dashboards and Agent Context. Authorized database text and Gmail content enter the Knowledge Ingestion and Memory path with source versions, customer/project scope, timestamps, deletion propagation and permission metadata. Memory here means retrievable project history, not model training or a shared cross-customer memory. Structured facts use permission-checked SQL; documents use controlled retrieval. The authenticated user's customer, project and document permissions are resolved by trusted backend code and enforced before retrieval; the model cannot choose or remove those constraints. Returned records are reauthorized before prompt assembly, with minimal necessary fields, masking where required and source references. Cortex Search uses owner's rights: underlying table permissions must not be assumed to automatically enforce caller isolation. A trusted retrieval service enforces mandatory ACL filters and restricted service credentials, with separate indexes/services where required by the security boundary. Customer/project scopes also apply to caches and memory; revocations and deletions invalidate derived retrieval copies. Only approved model endpoints may receive this context. A Cortex Search deployment and its embedding/reranking models must meet the approved cloud processing policy. Search freshness is tracked separately from raw ingestion; publication does not imply that an asynchronous search index is already refreshed. No end-to-end zero-latency or exactly-once transport guarantee is made. All visible labels are English. Blue processing, grey checks, green publication, 32-pixel platform marks and orthogonal arrows follow the existing Agent Eval, Risk Model and Multi-Agent drill-downs. No other architecture diagram is changed.
